chunks: From him, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Hamdan al-Qalanisi, from Ishaq ibn Bunan, from Ibn Baqqah, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), when the one to be kept apart (al-mu'allā) refused to divorce, would make for him a pen of reeds and give him a quarter of his sustenance until he divorced.

key_terms.الْمُؤَلَّى: One confined for refusal to divorce
key_terms.رُبُعَ قُوتِهِ: A quarter of his sustenance/food allowance

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for a husband who refuses to divorce his wife in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar details the specific mechanism of 'al-mu'allā' (confinement for refusal to divorce), where a recalcitrant husband is confined in a reed enclosure ('hazirah') and sustained on a quarter of his provisions until he consents to the divorce. It highlights the practical judicial authority of the Imam or judge to enforce marital dissolution through economic pressure and physical seclusion, ensuring the wife is not held hostage by the husband's stubbornness.
